<!-- pr-reviewer: b3dd4934090d6d30e17a1130939f6789799f8f2a -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge**

Thanks @seelesturm - a clear, well-scoped fix.

**What looks good**
- The inter-hole refusal now needs all three: distinct boundary loops, a positive gap no wider than the cutter, and a missing row piece. Everything else is not refused but goes through the unchanged radius-grown clipping, so it can only leave material unfaced and reported in the swept-area note. A misclassified concave return never routes a move through material (`face_holes.rs` `narrow_gap`, `crossings`).
- Both sides of the boundary are pinned in `face_concave_holes.rs`: wide and narrow U-notches in both cut directions (no false refusal), and the exactly-one-tool-wide distinct-hole case, which still refuses. The existing `face_holes` control is kept.
- No new unwrap/expect/panic in non-test code (the remaining `expect`s in `face_holes.rs` are in the test module). Comparisons are on f64 with no new casts or indexing. Provenance and gate-map headers are present. Files stay under 400 lines (face.rs 310, face_holes.rs 254, new test 131).
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/260-facing-gap.md` (not RECOMMENDED.md). The body has a `Changelog:` line and ends `Fixes #260`. No build.rs, scripts, workflow or dependency changes. CHANGELOG.md is untouched.

**Local results (trial merge with current origin/main, clean, no conflicts)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-motion --lib` | 149 passed |
| `center_cut_owed` | 7 passed |
| `face_blend` | 8 passed |
| `face_concave_holes` | 3 passed |
| `face_holes` | 6 passed |
| `clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The refusal message wording changed from "narrower than" to "no wider than" the tool, matching the new `<=` rule. Good.
- Gaps between separate holes that are wider than the cutter and have no row piece are no longer refused; they fall to the unfaced-area note. That is consistent with the Prime Directive (visible, not silent) but is a small behaviour widening worth knowing about.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
